title: Books and films
subtitle: novel, thriller, director, reviews
summary: Talk about the books you read and the films you watch, and use the right words for writers, actors and directors.

lesson.heading: Kinds of book
rows: stories about imaginary people and events
an exciting story, often about crime
the story of a person's life, written by another person
pieces of creative writing in short lines

lesson.heading: Reading
lesson.text: Many people start with **fiction** and read hundreds of **novels**, mostly **thrillers** and **science fiction**. Later they may move on to **biographies** and even some **poetry**.

examples.text: My favourite **author** is John le Carre.
I have started reading quite a lot of **biographies**.
Two of my favourite **poets** are Antonio Machado and Federico Garcia Lorca.
They both wrote **poems** in the early 20th century.

lesson.note: A biography is written by another person. A book someone writes about their own life is an autobiography.

lesson.heading: Kinds of film
rows: a film that makes people frightened, e.g. Dracula
a comedy that has a love story
an exciting film, often about crime

lesson.heading: Choosing a film
lesson.text: People decide what to see in different ways. Some read **reviews** - opinions in a newspaper or magazine. Others look for a big **star**, a famous **actor**. Some just want **entertainment**: things you see or do to enjoy yourself.

examples.text: If a film gets good **reviews**, then I often go and see it.
If there's a big **star** in it, then I am more likely to see it.
I'm not interested in films that are serious or **complicated**.

lesson.heading: What's on?
lesson.text: **What's on?** means 'What films are being shown at the cinema?'. If you want to see something, you can say informally that you **fancy** seeing it. The **latest** film means the newest, most recent one.

examples.text: I look to see **what's on** and go to anything that I **fancy** seeing.
There's the **latest** film by Pedro Almodovar. It only came out yesterday.
For me the film **director** is the most important thing.
examples.note: the director tells the actors what to do

examples.text: I always go and see the **latest** film by directors I really like.

lesson.text: A *poem* is one piece of writing; *poetry* is the art in general. Say *I read a poem*, not ~~I read a poetry~~.

exercises.prompt: Match each kind of book or film with its description.

pairs.right: an exciting story, often about crime
the story of a person's life by another person
a film that makes people frightened
a funny film with a love story

exercises.statement: Many poems are around 300 pages long.
exercises.explanation: Many novels are around 300 pages long. Poems are short pieces of writing in lines.

exercises.prompt: Cinema grew in popularity in the first half of the 20th ___.
exercises.explanation: A century is a period of 100 years.

exercises.prompt: I enjoy science fiction because I like stories about the ___.
exercises.explanation: Science fiction tells stories about the future.

exercises.prompt: What's ___ at the cinema this week?
exercises.explanation: What's on? asks which films are being shown.

exercises.prompt: We went to see the film because there was a good ___ in the newspaper.
exercises.explanation: A review gives an opinion about a film or a book.

exercises.prompt: William Wordsworth is a very famous ___.
exercises.explanation: A poet is a person who writes poetry.

exercises.prompt: I thought the film was good ___.
exercises.explanation: Entertainment is things you see or do to enjoy yourself.

exercises.prompt: I thought the ___ in the film was a bit unnatural.
exercises.explanation: Acting is what actors do; the actor is the person.

exercises.prompt: I didn't agree with what the ___ said about the new film.
exercises.explanation: A reviewer is the person who writes a review.

exercises.prompt: Put each word into the right group.
categories: A kind of writing or film

exercises.prompt: *A:* Oh, Almodovar - the man who ___ Julieta? *B:* Yes, that's him.
exercises.explanation: A director directs a film: he or she tells the actors what to do.

exercises.prompt: He's a very good director, but I don't understand some of his films - they're a bit ___ for me.
*A:* It's a film based on the ___ by Khaled Hosseini. It's a very good book. *B:* I'd love to see it.
exercises.explanation: A novel is a long book of fiction; many films are based on novels.

exercises.prompt: Ask a friend informally whether they want to see a particular film.
exercises.answer: Do you fancy seeing that film?
exercises.explanation: Fancy doing something is an informal way of saying want to do it.
